draft.title: Dilution
card: Diluting a solution means adding solvent, usually water. The solution gets a larger volume and a lower concentration.
The amount of solute does not change, because only water is added. The moles of solute before dilution equal the moles after.
Since n = cV, the moles before are c₁V₁ and the moles after are c₂V₂. So c₁V₁ = c₂V₂.
Use the same units for volume on both sides, such as mL or L. The final volume V₂ is the total volume, not the volume of water added.
draft.remember: Water changes the volume and concentration, but not the moles of solute.

a.q: A student adds water to a sodium chloride solution. What stays the same?
opts: The total volume of the solution
The mass of the whole solution
a.why: Only water is added, so the amount of solute is unchanged. Concentration falls because the same moles are now in a larger volume.
a.clue: Think about what is added and what is not.

b.q: Priya has 50 mL of 2.0 mol/L hydrochloric acid. She adds water to make a final volume of 250 mL. What is the new concentration?
b.why: c₂ = c₁V₁ ÷ V₂ = (2.0 × 50) ÷ 250 = 0.40 mol/L. The tempting 0.50 mol/L comes from using 200 mL, the water added, as V₂, but V₂ is the final total volume.
b.clue: V₂ is the total volume at the end, not the water added.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: the moles of solute stay the same, and (2.0 × 50) ÷ 250 = 0.40 mol/L.
